## Why Multi-Target Container Compilation Matters

Modern R projects span diverse deployment targets:

- **Reproducible Quarto manuscripts** combining R, Python (`reticulate`/Jupyter), LaTeX PDF output, and spatial or graphics libraries (`sf`, `ragg`).
- **Production Shiny applications** requiring non-root containers, HTTP health checks, background async workers (`mirai`/`promises`), and a reverse proxy.
- **HPC Bayesian & compiled pipelines** (`cmdstanr`, `RTMB`, `rjags`, `Rcpp`, `rextendr`) where university clusters run **Apptainer / Singularity** rather than rootful Docker.

`rcapsule` compiles all three targets from a single static project scan and verifies every emitted specification against its built-in security and reproducibility linter.

## 1. Quarto Manuscript with LaTeX, Python, and Stan

```{r quarto-example}
library(rcapsule)

q_dir <- tempfile("rcapsule_quarto_demo_")
dir.create(q_dir)

writeLines(
  c(
    "project:",
    "  type: manuscript",
    "format:",
    "  pdf:",
    "    pdf-engine: pdflatex"
  ),
  file.path(q_dir, "_quarto.yml")
)

writeLines(
  c(
    "---",
    "title: 'Spatial Bayesian Modeling Manuscript'",
    "format: pdf",
    "---",
    "",
    "```{r}",
    "library(sf)",
    "library(ragg)",
    "library(ggplot2)",
    "```",
    "",
    "```{python}",
    "import numpy as np",
    "```",
    "",
    "```{stan}",
    "parameters { real alpha; }",
    "model { alpha ~ normal(0, 1); }",
    "```"
  ),
  file.path(q_dir, "manuscript.qmd")
)
writeLines(c("numpy==1.26.4", "scipy==1.13.0"), file.path(q_dir, "requirements.txt"))

sc_q <- scan_project(q_dir)
sc_q

df_q <- compile_dockerfile(sc_q, r_version = "4.4.1")
lint_container_spec(df_q)
cat(paste(df_q$lines[1:45], collapse = "\n"))
```

Notice how `compile_dockerfile()` automatically resolves `libgdal-dev`, `libgeos-dev`, `libproj-dev`, `libfreetype6-dev`, Quarto CLI, TinyTeX, a Python virtual environment (`--no-cache-dir`), and CmdStan in cache-optimal layers.

## 2. Production Shiny + Async Worker + Reverse Proxy Stack

When `scan_project()` detects a Shiny application (`app.R` or `ui.R`/`server.R`) alongside async workers (`worker.R`, `mirai`, `promises`), `compile_compose()` generates a hardened three-service stack (`app`, `worker`, and a pinned `caddy:2.8.4-alpine` reverse proxy) with `no-new-privileges`, health checks, and resource limits:

```{r shiny-example}
s_dir <- tempfile("rcapsule_shiny_demo_")
dir.create(s_dir)

writeLines(
  c(
    "library(shiny)",
    "library(bslib)",
    "library(mirai)",
    "ui <- page_sidebar(title = 'Forecast Dashboard', sidebar = sidebar('Inputs'), 'Plot')",
    "server <- function(input, output, session) {}",
    "shinyApp(ui, server)"
  ),
  file.path(s_dir, "app.R")
)
writeLines("library(mirai)\ndaemons(2)", file.path(s_dir, "worker.R"))

sc_s <- scan_project(s_dir)
comp_s <- compile_compose(sc_s, port = 3838L, proxy_port = 8080L)
lint_container_spec(comp_s)
cat(comp_s$content)
```

## 3. Bayesian & Compiled HPC Recipe for Apptainer

On university HPC clusters where Docker is unavailable, `compile_apptainer()` produces an Apptainer `.def` recipe complete with `Bootstrap: docker`, pinned base tags, `set -euo pipefail`, HPC bind directories (`/scratch`, `/work`, `/data`), non-root read permissions, `%runscript`, and `%test`:

```{r hpc-example}
h_dir <- tempfile("rcapsule_hpc_demo_")
dir.create(file.path(h_dir, "src"), recursive = TRUE)

writeLines(
  c(
    "library(cmdstanr)",
    "library(RTMB)",
    "library(Rcpp)",
    "m <- cmdstanr::cmdstan_model('model.stan')"
  ),
  file.path(h_dir, "run.R")
)
writeLines("parameters { real mu; } model { mu ~ normal(0, 1); }", file.path(h_dir, "model.stan"))
writeLines("#include <Rcpp.h>", file.path(h_dir, "src", "kernel.cpp"))

sc_h <- scan_project(h_dir)
def_h <- compile_apptainer(sc_h, r_version = "4.4.1")
lint_container_spec(def_h)
cat(def_h$content)
```

## 4. Static Auditing of Hand-Written Container Specs

`lint_container_spec()` can also audit existing hand-written Dockerfiles, Compose files, or Apptainer definitions to catch reproducibility and security pitfalls before deployment:

```{r lint-bad}
problematic_dockerfile <- c(
  "FROM rocker/r-ver:latest",
  "ENV API_KEY=hardcoded_token_value",
  "RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y libgdal-dev",
  "COPY . /app",
  "RUN Rscript -e \"renv::restore()\""
)

lint_container_spec(problematic_dockerfile, type = "dockerfile")
```

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(c(q_dir, s_dir, h_dir), recursive = TRUE)
```
